strengths: Addresses a real and important problem in knowledge editing with clear motivation grounded in the Linear Representation Hypothesis
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 3 models and 2 datasets with extensive metrics, ablations, and large-scale experiments (5,000 edits)
Strong empirical results with substantial improvements in specificity (+43.2 points on LLaMA-3-8B) while maintaining efficacy and generalization
Thorough analysis section validating subspace hypotheses through variance analysis, component decomposition, and empirical testing (Section 6.2)
Clear visualization of reduced perturbation at entity's last token compared to baselines (Figures 2-3)
Good reproducibility with detailed hyperparameters, implementation details, and promise to release code/data
Ablation study reveals synergistic interaction between key vector and residual vector components
Robust across contexts (CHED evaluation) and maintains stability in long-horizon editing settings
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: SVD-based subspace identification and gradient-based direction finding are standard techniques; main contribution is their combination rather than fundamental innovation

Fixed 2-dimensional subspace for residual vector δ' lacks rigorous justification—why exactly 2 dimensions? Assumes negligible interactions but provides no sensitivity analysis over dimensionality choices

Stated mechanism (w1 increases new object logit, w2 decreases old object logit) empirically doesn't hold—both directions affect both objectives. Authors acknowledge this but don't explain why the method still works despite mechanism mismatch
Generalization concerns: Entity-agnostic subspace K_s^⊥ identified from PARAREL may not generalize to different entity distributions at test time; no analysis of variation across entity types
Arbitrary hyperparameter choices: τ_energy=0.4 and λ=0.3 applied uniformly across models without per-model tuning or principled justification for these values
Missing statistical rigor: No confidence intervals, significance tests, or run-to-run variance despite ~1000 test cases per setting; differences lack statistical validation
Limited failure case analysis: No investigation of performance variation across edit difficulty levels or explanation of marginal improvements on some settings
Orthogonality assumption: Claim that w1^T w2 = 0 is verified post-hoc but not enforced during optimization—unclear how often assumption is violated or its impact
Conceptual gap: Distinguishing features via variance is intuitive but hand-wavy; high variance could indicate entity information worth preserving rather than irrelevant features
No computational cost comparison with baselines despite additional SVD and optimization requirements

Strong empirical results on COUNTERFACT with substantial specificity improvements (+43.2 points on LLaMA-3-8B) while maintaining efficacy
Convincing analysis demonstrating reduced perturbation at entity tokens and empirical validation of subspace hypotheses
Thorough evaluation including 5000-edit stability, context robustness (CHED), and general capability benchmarks
weaknesses: Limited novelty: straightforward application of SVD-based subspace decomposition without significant conceptual contribution beyond AlphaEdit
Weak theoretical justification for critical design choices, particularly the 2D subspace assumption for the residual vector and why entity-agnostic features specifically harm specificity
Inconsistent improvements across datasets (dramatic gains on COUNTERFACT but modest improvements on ZSRE), suggesting potential overfitting to COUNTERFACT characteristics
Hyperparameter sensitivity with clear tradeoffs between generalization and specificity (Figure 5), lacking principled guidance for setting τ_energy and λ in practice
Paper acknowledges w₁ and w₂ are not fully disentangled (overlapping effects) but does not adequately explore implications for the 2D decomposition model
General Capability degradation not adequately explained (e.g., GPT-J near-zero F1 on most benchmarks in Table 8)
Missing computational cost analysis and limited scope (only factual knowledge editing in locate-then-edit paradigm)
Table 4 finding that 24% norm component δ∥_W is more effective than 76% component δ⊥_W lacks compelling mechanistic explanation

strengths: Strong empirical results with substantial improvements in specificity (43.2 points over AlphaEdit on LLaMA-3-8B) while maintaining high efficacy, consistently across three model architectures

Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple datasets (COUNTERFACT, zsRE), diverse metrics (efficacy, generalization, specificity, fluency, consistency, general capability), and robustness tests (CHED, 5000-edit scalability)

Thorough analysis section with clear evidence for core hypotheses: last-token perturbation reduction (Section 6.1), entity-specific vs. entity-agnostic feature decomposition (Section 6.2.1), and critical subspace identification (Section 6.2.2)
Well-grounded methodology leveraging Linear Representation Hypothesis with reasonable assumptions about semantic feature decomposition
Strong reproducibility: promised code/data release, comprehensive hyperparameter documentation, and detailed experimental protocol
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (heatmaps, component analysis, tradeoff curves) and well-structured ablation study demonstrating synergy between components
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: individual components (SVD-based subspace identification, energy thresholding, subspace constraints) are standard techniques; primary contribution is their application to AlphaEdit, which is somewhat incremental

2D subspace assumption for residual vector δ' lacks strong justification: authors acknowledge w1 and w2 are not fully disentangled (Section 6.2.2), no ablation on dimensionality choice, and theoretical motivation is weakened by post-hoc validation via Table 4

Subspace analysis could be stronger: variance analysis (Table 2) shows only 2.6x-4.5x differences, and the claim that K⊥ₛ captures entity-agnostic features is validated indirectly through variance rather than direct validation of feature semantics

Simplified modeling choices: ignoring w1-w2 interactions (Appendix C) and assuming dimensionality without systematic justification reduce theoretical rigor, though empirical results suggest pragmatic validity

Scope limitations: only addresses MLP down-projection editing within locate-then-edit paradigm; unclear applicability to other editing methods (attention heads, LoRA) or knowledge types beyond Wikidata factual knowledge

Missing ablations and analyses: no comparison of subspace constraints applied to other baselines (RECT, PRUNE), unclear if per-model hyperparameter tuning would improve results, no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals
General capability degradation on some benchmarks (Table 8 shows near-zero F1 on select GPT-J/Qwen tasks) suggests potential side effects that deserve further investigation
Hyperparameter choices fixed across models without sensitivity validation: τenergy=0.4 and λ=0.3 held constant despite Figure 5 showing clear tradeoffs; unclear if these are optimal or require tuning

strengths: Strong empirical results with substantial specificity improvements (+43.2 points over AlphaEdit on LLaMA-3-8B)
Comprehensive experimental validation across three models, multiple datasets (COUNTERFACT, ZSRE, CHED), and large-scale settings (5,000 sequential edits)
Thorough analysis section rigorously validating hypotheses: variance analysis of entity-specific/agnostic components, direct perturbation measurements, component effect decomposition
Clear ablation study demonstrating synergy between key and residual vector constraints
Excellent reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters, implementation details, transparent cost analysis, promised code release
Well-motivated approach grounded in Linear Representation Hypothesis with clear subspace identification strategy
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily applies standard SVD-based subspace decomposition to existing AlphaEdit framework; incremental rather than conceptually novel contribution

Unjustified 2D dimensionality choice: no principled justification for why 2D is optimal for residual subspace; Table 4 shows δ∥W (24% of norm) is effective but doesn't prove 2D is better than 1D/3D/adaptive approaches

Incomplete component disentanglement: Figure 7 and §6.2.2 reveal w₁ also suppresses old object and w₂ promotes new object, contradicting the clean separation hypothesis; authors acknowledge this needs future work, undermining conceptual clarity
Orthogonal decomposition assumption lacks theoretical justification: why should entity-agnostic features be orthogonal to entity-specific ones? Choice is pragmatic but not principled
Energy threshold τ_energy appears somewhat arbitrary (0.4); while sensitivity analysis shows stability in 0.3-0.5 range, no principled method for setting on new architectures
ZSRE specificity evaluation modified from standard (using model outputs as reference rather than gold answers) because standard measurement 'is uninformative'; complicates cross-method comparison
Computational overhead: ~6000 seconds pre-computation time and 10,000 subject key vectors required; scalability to larger models and non-transformer architectures unexplored
Limited failure case analysis: no discussion of when SUIT performs poorly, or how it handles rare entities where entity-specific/agnostic distinction may be unclear
Simplified additive update (Appendix C) ignores w₁-w₂ interactions that empirically exist, simplifying a complex interaction pattern

strengths: Strong empirical results with substantial improvements in specificity (+43.2 points over AlphaEdit on LLaMA-3-8B CounterFact) while maintaining high efficacy
Comprehensive evaluation across multiple models, datasets, metrics, and settings (sequential editing, contextual robustness, ripple effects)

Thorough empirical validation of core hypotheses through variance analysis (Table 2), ablation studies (Table 5), hyperparameter sensitivity analysis (Figure 5), and perturbation analysis (Figures 2-3)
Extensive supplementary material with detailed experimental protocols, hyperparameter specifications, and additional analyses supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: the method combines standard techniques (SVD, PCA projection, gradient optimization) without introducing novel algorithms or algorithmic insights. It is primarily an engineering contribution applying known tools to knowledge editing

Weak theoretical justification for core design choices: (1) the 2D assumption for δ' lacks derivation and ablation; (2) the connection between high-variance components and entity-agnostic features is poorly explained and potentially conceptually confused; (3) τ_energy selection via harmonic mean S appears ad-hoc without principled motivation

Critical finding undermines core hypothesis: Figures 4 and Appendix G show w₁ also suppresses the old object and w₂ also promotes the new object, contradicting the stated design. Authors acknowledge this is 'not fully disentangled' but dismiss exploring it, suggesting the hypothesis may be incomplete or flawed

Evaluation fairness concerns: ZSRE specificity metric is modified from standard practice (comparing to model-generated tokens instead of gold objects). Table 6 shows AlphaEdit and SUIT have nearly identical results under the standard metric (32.7), meaning large improvements in Table 1 ZSRE results only appear with the custom metric, making fair comparison difficult

Significant preprocessing overhead not adequately reported: Appendix I shows 6,026.9 seconds (1.68 hours) per model-layer pair for constructing K_subject with 10,000 subjects. This ~8+ hour per-model cost is not required by baselines like AlphaEdit, but computational comparisons and fairness implications are not discussed

Incomplete subspace analysis: empirical validation shows K_s has higher variance (Table 2) but does not explain *why* removing K⊥_s benefits editing or whether partial retention might be better. No interpretability analysis of actual features captured by these subspaces

Missing ablations on key design choices: no ablation on 2D dimensionality selection (why not 1D, 3D, or adaptive?), no comparison of τ_energy selection methods, no sensitivity to penalty weight λ beyond Figure 5

Inconsistent evaluation across datasets: CounterFact uses standard argmax pre-knowledge criterion; ZSRE explicitly violates this (Section D.3) due to question format. This procedural inconsistency complicates cross-dataset interpretation
Limited failure analysis: no discussion of when SUIT fails, no error case studies, no comparison of failure modes with baselines

Confusing exposition in Section 4.2: the relationship between high-variance principal components and entity-agnostic features requires clarification. High variance across subjects could indicate entity-specific variation rather than agnosticity, but this is not adequately addressed

strengths: Strong empirical results with dramatic improvements in specificity (+43.2 points on LLaMA COUNTERFACT) while maintaining high efficacy
Well-motivated approach grounded in Linear Representation Hypothesis with clear intuition for why subspace decomposition reduces model perturbation

Exceptionally thorough analysis validating core hypotheses: variance analysis (Table 2) shows 2.6-4.5× higher variance in entity-specific components; update matrix minimally interacts with entity-agnostic space (Table 3); constrained residual is disproportionately effective (Table 4)
Comprehensive evaluation across three models, two datasets, multiple benchmarks (COUNTERFACT, ZSRE, CHED, RippleEdits), long-horizon stability (5K edits), and general capability preservation
Robust across models: energy threshold τenergy in [0.3-0.4] generalizes consistently (Appendix H); scales to larger models (LLaMA2-13B) without retuning
Clear ablation study (Table 5) demonstrating synergy between components: k′+δ′ (86.8) substantially outperforms k-only (82.2) or δ-only (68.3)
Strong reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters, computational cost analysis (Appendix I), promised code release, and extensive supplementary materials
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: paper essentially applies SVD and constrained optimization to modify AlphaEdit vectors—straightforward application of existing techniques rather than fundamental advance

Critical design choice lacks justification: 2D subspace assumption has no ablation (why not 1D, 3D?); section 6.2.2 reveals w₁ and w₂ are not fully disentangled (w₁ suppresses old object, w₂ promotes new); orthogonality assumption (w₁ᵀw₂=0) not empirically validated

Hyperparameter selection appears somewhat arbitrary: N=10K for Ksubject (Table 16 shows 0.81 similarity but no principled justification); τenergy selected via harmonic mean maximization on COUNTERFACT—while generalizable across models, methodology remains dataset-dependent with no guidance for truly new domains

Significant pre-computation overhead limits practical adoption: requires ~1.5 hours and 3.6GB VRAM per layer for LLaMA-3-8B (Table 15); requires PARAREL dataset access; setup costs may prohibit use in resource-constrained settings

ZSRE evaluation methodology undermines interpretability: paper acknowledges gold-answer partial credit is uninformative (pre-edit 32%, Table 6); authors use model's own outputs as reference instead—pragmatic but makes results non-comparable with future work and less convincing than COUNTERFACT results

Limited scope and generalization: evaluation on models up to 13B only (no 70B+ models where dynamics may differ); method is MLP-specific with unclear applicability to different architectures; no analysis of failure modes, edge cases, or which edit types benefit most from subspace approach

Design justifications lack rigor: no ablation on residual subspace dimensionality; no empirical validation of orthogonality assumption; paper acknowledges non-disentanglement but treats as minor ('worth exploring in future work')

Presentation could be tightened: 30-page paper with redundancy between main text and appendices; important design choices (why 2D? orthogonality?) insufficiently discussed in main text; some experimental details relegated to appendices
